definitions: To dig a trench or trenches in (land).
To cut a trench or channel in (something).
To encroach upon; to infringe on.
To dig a deep ditch or a series of ditches.
To make a trench or trenches.
To dig a trench around (a place or thing).
To make a trench in (soil) for drainage or irrigation.
To make a trench in (a road or other surface) to lay pipes, cables, etc.
examples: They will trench the field for better drainage.
The soldiers began to trench the area.
We need to trench the garden.
The workers will trench the road.
The river has trenched the valley over millennia.
He trenched the ground to plant the new hedge.
The utility company will trench the street to install new fibre optics.
The archaeologists carefully trenched the site.
Farmers often trench their fields to manage water.
The builders trenched the perimeter for the foundations.
